yarn-dinkum.authenticity: Reads like an Australian parent posting: "Turns out the missus has literally been stacking the deck for him", "He loves a game", "I dunno if she doesn't notice". "cos" and "red-hot go" are natural. Nothing stage-Australian.
yarn-dinkum.register: A steady light-to-moderate touch: "littlie", "missus", "squiz", "off with the fairies", "spewin'", "Chrissie", "red-hot go", "dunno". Slightly more than a level-2 sprinkling but no swearing.
yarn-dinkum.tone: Keeps the earnest, reflective parenting-forum tone: "Is that a fair worry at his age?" and the second poster's measured "That way a win's a real achievement for either of us".
yarn-dinkum.flow: Smooth and conversational: "Thing is, I noticed last night that he wins every single time." Splitting the long question into "Is that a fair worry at his age? Or is he just too little..." helps.
yarn-dinkum.variety: Varied terms with no tic leaned on: "squiz", "pops it", "off with the fairies", "spewin'", "heaps", "over the moon", "red-hot go". "cos" appears twice.
yarn-dinkum.essence: Unmistakably the original question and answer, with the same shape and argument: "What makes a kids' game a kids' game is that luck mostly counts for heaps more than strategy."

yarn-deadset.authenticity: Natural throughout: "He loves playing, but seems (to me, at least) more keen on the playing than the winning. I reckon that's perfect." "I dunno if she doesn't notice" sounds like a real speaker.
yarn-deadset.register: A light level-2 touch: "littlie", "squiz", "missus", "spewin'", "heaps", "Chrissie", "stoked", "dunno", in otherwise plain prose. No swearing.
yarn-deadset.tone: The earnest question and considered reply come through: "Is that a fair worry at his age, or is he just too young to care about the competitive side of games".
yarn-deadset.flow: Reads cleanly; the long question stays as one long sentence as in the original: "Is that a fair worry at his age, or is he just too young to care about the competitive side of games, and letting him win is nothing more than a harmless way to get him enjoying playing at this age?" yarn-troppo.meaning: All the points are there, but it adds claims and events: "So I start watching" (the original only noticed), "Card sharp, she is.", "Cold-blooded, that.", "(she's the dealer, course she is)", and a framing line "Then someone else pipes up". Most are colour hanging off the original; "So I start watching" is a small invented event.
yarn-troppo.sense: Mostly fits: "off with the fairies", "spewin' the first time he doesn't", "over the moon", "red-hot go". "get him hooked on a game" strains 'incentive to enjoy playing', and "it stops being fun, quick smart" stretches "quick smart" (promptly, at once) a bit.
yarn-troppo.authenticity: Lively and mostly local: "this one's been doin' my head in", "Nothing flash.", "cop disappointment". But some lines feel performed: "Just happy to be there, bless him." (more British), "when does it become one, ay?".
yarn-troppo.register: Heavier than level 2, a chatty yarn: "Now, this one's been doin' my head in.", "Card sharp, she is.", "Mate, what makes a kids' game a kids' game", "Poor little bloke.", "quick smart". No swearing.
yarn-troppo.tone: The original is a sincere question; E plays the wife's trick for laughs ("Cold-blooded, that.", "Card sharp, she is.") and the reply's measured advice gets breezy ("Poor little bloke." and "Earned it."). The earnest core still comes through.
yarn-troppo.flow: Punchy and readable, though the fragments stack up: "Except. Last night it dawns on me: the kid never loses. Not once." and "she goes, she reckons he should win".
yarn-troppo.variety: Wide range of slang and openers: "doin' my head in", "Nothing flash", "squiz", "off with the fairies", "rocking up", "pipes up", "red-hot go", "quick smart", "cop disappointment". Some reliance on short tag sentences ("Not once.", "Earned it.", "Cold-blooded, that.").
yarn-troppo.essence: Recognisably the original question and reply, though the retelling as a comic yarn and the framing "Then someone else pipes up" shift its character from forum Q&A to anecdote.
